clue.text: A girl's ring? It shows yours was wasted

definitions.meaning: an engagement ring on a girl's finger signals that she is promised in marriage
the busy tone on a telephone tells the caller their ring went nowhere

explanation.surface: A rueful comment on a girl's ring and a wasted effort.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase covers both a betrothal token on the finger and the busy tone heard on a telephone line.

clue.text: Did she finally aspire to be Galatea?

definitions.text: Did she finally aspire to be Galatea?

parts.words: Did she finally aspire to be Galatea?
parts.note: Shaw's flower girl, the Galatea of his Pygmalion, at last learns to sound her aitches, to aspirate them

explanation.surface: A question about a woman longing to become the statue brought to life in myth.
explanation.definitionFit: Shaw's heroine in Pygmalion is the modern counterpart of Galatea, and her lessons teach her to pronounce her H sounds.

clue.text: Gallery containing no merchandise

indicators.note: the gallery word holds the zero within itself

parts.note: the gods are the highest gallery of seats in a theatre
O is nought, a zero

explanation.surface: An art gallery with nothing to sell.
explanation.definitionFit: Merchandise is wares or stock for sale, things traded.

clue.text: Gold a siren converts into jewelled earrings

indicators.note: converts says the letters of the three words before it are changed into a new form

explanation.surface: A mermaid-like siren turns gold into fancy earrings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'converts' rearranges GOLD, A and SIREN; 'into' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Girandoles are ornate pendant earrings, often set with stones around a central gem.

clue.text: Bill is in the valley willing to go out with him?

definitions.text: willing to go out with him?

indicators.note: the bill word sits inside the valley word

parts.note: a dale is a valley
a tab is a bill, as in picking up the tab

explanation.surface: Bill lives down in the valley; is she keen to date him?
explanation.definitionFit: Someone datable is fit to be taken on a romantic outing.

clue.text: Imaginative understanding of Society in one dark period

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: the society abbreviation goes within the dark period

parts.note: night is the dark part of the day

explanation.surface: A grand phrase about society's understanding during a dark era.
explanation.walkthrough: S is put after the N of NIGHT, giving NSIGHT, after I.
explanation.definitionFit: Insight is perceptive grasp of the inner nature of something.

clue.text: Pinch? It means prison

explanation.surface: A petty thief is told that a theft will mean jail.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are British slang: to steal something, and the police cells or jail.

clue.text: Party time — high spot: for Bolivar?

parts.note: Lib is short for Liberal, a political party
an era is a period of time
a tor is a rocky hilltop

explanation.surface: A political party gathers at a high point in honour of the South American hero.
explanation.walkthrough: Simón Bolívar was hailed as El Libertador for freeing much of South America from Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: Bolívar's title means the freer, the man who released nations from colonial rule.

clue.text: Like Bob Major, for example affected by a negative sound

parts.note: camp means theatrically affected
no is a negative reply
a sound argument is logical

explanation.surface: Someone called Bob Major is mannered, swayed by a negative noise.
explanation.walkthrough: Bob Major is a method in change ringing of church bells, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: Campanology is the art of bell-ringing, and Bob Major is one of its ringing methods.

clue.text: Athenian, orator I call for help about a case

indicators.note: the distress call goes round the box word

parts.note: SOS is the distress signal
a crate is a packing case

explanation.surface: An Athenian speaker cries for help over a legal case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts the box inside the distress call; 'I' is taken as written, and the definition names a speech-writer of classical Athens.
explanation.definitionFit: Isocrates was a celebrated speech-writer and teacher of rhetoric in classical Athens.

clue.text: A horse-god in Egypt has a serpent

parts.note: a cob is a sturdy short-legged horse
Ra is the Egyptian sun god

explanation.surface: In Egypt a deity shaped like a horse keeps a snake.
explanation.walkthrough: The leading 'A' and 'has a' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: A cobra is a venomous hooded snake, the serpent on pharaohs' crowns.

clue.text: Old admiral not known outside the south

indicators.note: the word for unknown sits around the compass letter

parts.note: anon, anonymous, means of unknown name

explanation.surface: An obscure old naval commander never known beyond the south.
explanation.walkthrough: George Anson was an 18th-century British admiral who sailed round the world.
explanation.definitionFit: Lord Anson commanded a British fleet on a famous circumnavigation in the 1740s.

clue.text: Claim a large amount

definitions.meaning: to bag something is to stake a claim to it

explanation.surface: Staking a claim to a great deal.
explanation.definitionFit: British informal usage: to reserve first dibs on something, and lots, as in plenty of time.

clue.text: Bit back, using the mouth

indicators.note: back says the word for a bit is read in reverse

parts.note: a part is a bit, a portion

explanation.surface: Biting backwards with one's mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: Trap is slang for mouth, as in shut your trap.

clue.text: In a garden, every climber can : be a non-poisonous plant

annotationWithheld.why: In a garden, every climber can be a non-poisonous plant (scan; OCR adds a colon): no parse gives BELLADONNA, which is poisonous, and no wordplay is visible
annotationWithheld.clue: In a garden, every climber can : be a non-poisonous plant

clue.text: Result in error -now then!

parts.note: out means mistaken, as in your sums are out
come, as in come now, is a mild remonstrance

explanation.surface: Someone is told off after a mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: An outcome is the consequence or end-product of events.

clue.text: Position of guardian in Proust is hard to change

indicators.note: to change says the letters of the author's name and the short word are reordered

parts.note: the author's name plus the short word, printed is but needing it
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Proust has trouble shifting from his role as someone's guardian.
explanation.walkthrough: As printed, PROUST IS H has two Ss and one T, so the anagram fails: the setter or printer slipped and wrote 'is' for 'it'.
explanation.definitionFit: Tutorship is the office of a tutor, in law a guardian of a minor.

clue.text: Slit is in fashion in: new jersey, as stated

indicators.note: the slit word goes inside the fashion word

parts.note: ton is fashion or style, as in bon ton
a rent is a slit or tear

explanation.surface: A slit is the fashion in a new jumper, so it is claimed.
explanation.walkthrough: A jersey is a jumper (British for a sweater). The definition plays on 'state': Trenton is the capital of the US state of New Jersey.
explanation.definitionFit: Trenton is the capital city of the American state of New Jersey.

clue.text: Post employs four

parts.note: mail is the sense, while the word post itself uses four of the alphabet's characters

explanation.surface: The Post Office hires four people.
explanation.definitionFit: Post is mail, the correspondence delivered, and the word post is spelt with four characters.

clue.text: Pointedly deceitful about a heavenly instrument

indicators.note: the word for deceitful goes round the instrument

parts.note: sly means cunning or deceitful
the harp is the instrument angels play in heaven

explanation.surface: Someone is sharply cunning about an angel's harp.
explanation.definitionFit: Sharply means pointedly, said with a cutting edge.

clue.text: A hypnotic, hymn tune grips many

indicators.note: the hymn word holds the Roman numeral inside it

parts.note: a choral, also chorale, is a hymn tune
L, the Roman numeral 50, stands for many

explanation.surface: A mesmerising hymn tune grips a huge crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: Chloral hydrate is a sedative drug that induces sleep.

clue.text: More transparent, so easier to understand

explanation.surface: Something see-through is more easily grasped.
explanation.definitionFit: The comparative means both more see-through, like glass, and plainer in meaning.

clue.text: Breach of duty in law or in race

indicators.note: the word or sits inside the race letters

parts.note: the TT, Tourist Trophy, is the motorcycle race on the Isle of Man

explanation.surface: A legal question of breach of duty, in law or in a race.
explanation.definitionFit: A tort is a civil wrong for which damages can be claimed.

clue.text: Price that has to be paid for getting on

definitions.text: Price that has to be paid for getting on

parts.words: Price that has to be paid for getting on
parts.note: the sum a passenger pays to board a bus or train, also hinting at how one gets on in life

explanation.surface: A remark on the cost of success.
explanation.definitionFit: A fare is the charge for a journey, and to fare is to get on or manage.

clue.text: Remove trousers, setting bad example

indicators.note: setting means arranging, so the letters are put in a new order

parts.note: EG is the abbreviation for example

explanation.surface: Someone taking their trousers off sets a poor example.
explanation.walkthrough: DEBAG is British slang, from student pranks, for pulling someone's trousers off.
explanation.definitionFit: Debag is old British slang for taking a person's trousers off as a prank.

clue.text: Instructions for a particular case

parts.note: a legal case: a barrister receives written instructions from a solicitor for it

explanation.surface: Guidance for a specific situation.
explanation.definitionFit: A brief is the solicitor's summary of a case given to counsel, and more widely any set of instructions.

clue.text: I dashed off to the country

parts.note: ran means dashed or hurried off

explanation.surface: Someone hurries off abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: Iran is the Middle Eastern nation formerly called Persia.

clue.text: There were smiles in his land

definitions.text: There were smiles in his land

parts.words: There were smiles in his land
parts.note: points to the composer of the operetta The Land of Smiles

explanation.surface: A happy country remembered.
explanation.definitionFit: Franz Lehár, the Hungarian composer, wrote the operetta Das Land des Lächelns, The Land of Smiles.

clue.text: Deluded person in a panic or a turmoil

indicators.note: turmoil means disorder, so the letters are thrown into confusion

explanation.surface: Someone deluded is in a panic or in turmoil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link; 'turmoil' scrambles A PANIC OR A.
explanation.definitionFit: A paranoiac suffers from paranoia, delusions of persecution or grandeur.

clue.text: It was a d — awful book of stories

parts.note: d was the abbreviation for an old British penny, from the Latin denarius
awful means dreadful

explanation.surface: Someone swears mildly about a terrible storybook.
explanation.walkthrough: The dash makes 'd — awful' look like a censored oath; d stood for a penny in British money before 1971. 'It was a' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Victorian cheap sensational serial fiction cost a penny and was famously lurid.
